summary: Dixie Butte R-6 ground cab (1968) in the Malheur National Forest, built after a 1967 windstorm; staffed in summer, reached by rough Forest Road 2610.

facts.design: 15 by 15 foot R-6 flat-top ground cab (present); earlier L-4 ground house from 1935

access.note: Reached by rough Forest Road 2610. No closure or permit requirement found in the pages read. The cab is staffed in summer and in active service.

visit.trail_note: Forest Road 2610 is rough and rocky; high-clearance vehicles recommended for washouts and gullies. A 2024 visitor drove about four miles and walked the rest. Check with the Prairie City Ranger District before a visit.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Malheur National Forest (Prairie City Ranger District)

events.note: Cabin with a rooftop platform built around 1911; a lookout on the butte was connected by telephone to the central office
New lookout building completed, reported by Independence Enterprise as best equipped on the reserve
L-4 ground house replaced the cupola cabin of the early 1920s
Lookout reported four forest fires within two days; crews sent from Sumpter
Observer spotted smoke 45 miles to the southwest and phoned the location to the John Day office; found to be a small slash fire
Windstorm damaged the structure in the fall of 1967
Present R-6 flat-top cab built, replacing the damaged structure

corrections.proposed: remove; no source found for a cab height
corrections.why: None of the pages read gives a height for the cab. The register gives the floor size (15 by 15 feet), not a height, so the 3.7 m figure has no support.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls the first lookout a cupola cabin of the early 1920s. Forest Lookouts and Cheryl Hill date a rooftop-platform cabin to about 1911 and a cupola to the 1920s. These are different structures on the same summit, so both are kept.
The register gives 7,511 feet (2,289 m), which matches the brief. Rex's page and Cheryl Hill give 7,592 feet. Both are reported in the story; no elevation fact key is set.

sources.title: Dixie Butte - Every Lookout in Oregon

notes_for_editor: Brief's height_m 3.7 has no source in the pages read and is proposed for removal. The 1968 present-cab date is consistent across NHLR, Rex's page and Trails Offroad. Elevation conflict left open: NHLR 7,511 ft vs 7,592 ft on Rex's page and Cheryl Hill. Staffing is from Rex's page (undated, every summer) and a July 2024 visit; current season not confirmed. Name spellings differ across accounts for the 1916 observer (Noey vs Noah Blaine), so no name is used. Forest Lookouts' newspaper items were read as quoted on that site, not from the originals. Trails Offroad is a paid trail-guide site; only its free text was used. Dixie Butte is not on the Malheur NF rental list, which names Fall Mountain Lookout. No new photos recorded. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the L-4 house replaced a cupola cabin of the early 1920s (NHLR), not several early cabins; the 1916 observer phoned the fire's point location, which the story now says.
